stemBlocks.value: Solve the simultaneous equations 2x + y = 3 and 5x − 2y = 12.
Think first: The y coefficients are 1 and −2, so doubling the first equation lines them up for elimination.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p097-q01 from workbook page 97.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply the first equation by 2 to match the y coefficients.
Add this to the second equation so that +2y and −2y cancel.
Substitute x = 2 into the simpler original equation.
Check in the equation you did not use.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply the first equation by 2 so the y terms cancel when the equations are added, solve for x, then substitute back.

whyThisWorks.value: Two linear equations describe two straight lines, and the solution is the single point where they cross. Adding a multiple of one equation to the other produces a new equation with the same solution but only one unknown, which can be solved directly.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding when the signs are the same, so nothing cancels.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding when the signs are the same, so nothing cancels.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying only the left-hand side of an equation by 2.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying only the left-hand side of an equation by 2.

commonErrors.misconception: Finding x correctly then substituting it into a mis-copied equation.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Finding x correctly then substituting it into a mis-copied equation.

examTip.value: Always substitute your answers into the equation you did not use for the substitution — it is a free, complete check.
